heroHeadline: Day 139: MOU Collapses — Iran Declares 'Existential War' After IRGC Strikes Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan; US Launches 7-Hour Strike Wave, Expands North; UAE Tankers Hit; Khamenei Funeral Draws Millions
heroSubtitle: Day 139 (July 16, 2026): The Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, signed June 17 by Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian with Pakistan mediating, collapsed after a July 6-7 wave of Iranian strikes on four commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. Trump declared the MOU 'over' on July 8 and resumed US strikes on Iranian territory (Bushehr, Chabahar, Bandar Abbas, Jask — 14 killed, 78 injured) plus a naval blockade of Iranian ports effective July 14. Three further tanker-attack waves followed (July 7, 11, 14), killing at least 2 tanker crew and wounding 8+. On July 15, IRGC struck US assets in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan overnight; Iran's top negotiator Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf declared the country in an 'essential and existential war with America' and the MOU void. The US responded with a seven-hour strike wave overnight into July 16, expanding into northern Iran, while Iran's military said it disabled two blockade-running tankers hours after the UAE reported Iranian missiles struck two of its own tankers in Omani waters. Iran's July death toll stands at 35+ killed, 300+ wounded; US military deaths reached 14 (including 6 killed in a KC-135 crash in Iraq on July 8-9), with Iran's disputed claim of 3 more US deaths in Kuwait (July 13) unconfirmed. In Lebanon, the Israel-Hezbollah front remained volatile despite a nominal June 19 ceasefire renewal — a June 18 strike on Nabatieh, Sidon, and Tyre killed 47, the war's deadliest single day on that front, and Hezbollah rejected a US-mediated 'lasting peace' framework on June 27. Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has not appeared publicly since succeeding his father, who was killed in the war's opening strike; he did not attend his father's multi-day state funeral in Tehran (July 3-9), which drew millions of mourners. Brent crude closed at ~$85/bbl on July 16, up sharply from a ~$77-80/bbl trough in late June as fighting resumed; Strait of Hormuz shipping traffic has again collapsed to 10-14 vessels/day. Washington's stated terms to end hostilities: Iran must declare all Hormuz channels open toll-free, halt attacks on shipping, and surrender its highly enriched uranium stockpile.
